_note: SAMPLE DATA. Two practice problems per site, written as short original paraphrases (not copied statements). Solutions are AI-style samples for offline testing.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.statement: Sample paraphrase: you climb a staircase of n steps, moving 1 or 2 steps at a time. Count the different ways to reach the top.
problems.summary:
Count the ways to climb n steps taking 1 or 2 steps at a time.
The answer follows the Fibonacci pattern.
problems.approach: The ways to reach step i are the ways to reach step i-1 plus the ways to reach step i-2. Keep only the last two values while walking up to n.

steps.title: Find the pattern
steps.explanation: The last move is either 1 step or 2 steps, so ways(i) = ways(i-1) + ways(i-2).

steps.title: Set the base cases
steps.explanation: There is 1 way to stand at step 0 and 1 way to reach step 1.

steps.title: Walk up the stairs
steps.explanation: Shift the pair forward n-1 times, adding the two previous counts each time.

edge_cases: large n stays fast because only two numbers are kept

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.statement: Sample paraphrase: given wall heights along a line, pick two walls that hold the most water between them.
problems.summary:
Choose two lines from an array of heights that trap the largest area.
Area is the shorter height times the distance between them.
problems.approach: Start with pointers at both ends and record the area. Move the pointer at the shorter wall inward, because moving the taller one can never increase the area.

steps.title: Start wide
steps.explanation: Put one pointer at each end: this is the widest container.

steps.title: Move the shorter wall
steps.explanation: The shorter wall limits the area, so only moving it can help.

edge_cases: equal heights: moving either side is fine

problems.title: Add Two Numbers
problems.statement: Sample paraphrase: for each of T test cases, read two integers and print their sum.
problems.summary:
Read T pairs of integers.
Print the sum of each pair on its own line.
problems.approach: Read the number of test cases, then read each pair and print the sum. Use fast input because T can be large.
problems.code:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    t = int(data[0])
    out = []
    for i in range(t):
        a, b = int(data[1 + 2 * i]), int(data[2 + 2 * i])
        out.append(str(a + b))
    print("\n".join(out))

main()
problems.complexity: O(T) time, O(T) space for the output.

problems.title: Reverse The Number
problems.statement: Sample paraphrase: for each test case, print the digits of N in reverse order without leading zeros.
problems.summary:
Reverse the digits of each given number.
Leading zeros in the result are dropped.
problems.approach: Reverse the number's string and convert it back to an integer, which removes leading zeros. Do this for every test case.
problems.code:
t = int(input())
for _ in range(t):
    n = input().strip()
    print(int(n[::-1]))
problems.complexity: O(d) time per number, where d is the number of digits.

problems.title: Kadane's Algorithm
problems.statement: Sample paraphrase: find the largest sum of any non-empty contiguous part of an integer array.
problems.summary:
Find the maximum sum over all contiguous subarrays.
The array can contain negative numbers.
problems.approach: Walk the array keeping the best sum of a subarray that ends here: either extend the previous one or start fresh. Track the largest value seen.

problems.title: Missing Number in Array
problems.statement: Sample paraphrase: an array holds n-1 distinct numbers from 1 to n. Find the one that is missing.
problems.summary:
Numbers 1 to n appear once each, except one.
Return the missing number.
problems.approach: The sum 1 + 2 + ... + n is n(n+1)/2. Subtract the array's sum from it to get the missing number.
problems.code:
def missing_number(arr, n):
    return n * (n + 1) // 2 - sum(arr)
